evidence: Read instruction.md cold. It opens as a person's request ('Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?', line 1), states the stakes with a reason ('Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts', line 1), and expresses requirements as first-person needs with reasons ('I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none', line 3; 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor', line 5; 'They must never see our internal notes...', line 9). No numbered acceptance list, no shall/must table, no feature matrix: modal count in instruction.md is must x2, mustn't x1, should x2, and no bulleted or numbered lines. Line 11 hands off detail to the notes and leaves layout/names to the builder ('layout and names are yours'). Line 13 is the lesson-5 self-check ask phrased naturally ('please check it yourself the way we'll use it'). Build-recipe check (quality-checks.md #1 defect): line 15 names Node.js/Express/SQLite, /app, server.js, port 3000, GET /api/health, /app/app.db and DB_PATH; these are the shared template runtime contract (template integration.md lines 3-10 states the same stack and facts) that row 4 requires to be stated, not a task-added recipe; file and route layout is explicitly left open ('How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call', line 15; integration.md line 14). Only one endpoint (the mandated health check) is named; no endpoint list or file layout is prescribed. Lines 17-19 (seed loading, accounts) are runtime facts in conversational form. Lesson 12 sweep over the notes (hireops_rules.md): written as 'How we run HireOps ... the working rules our recruiting team follows. Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are up to you' (lines 1-5). Rules carry user reasons throughout, e.g. 'We like to know where a card was when it was rejected, because reopening takes it back to exactly that stage' (50-51), 'Several of us work the same board, so...' (78), 'We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands' (126), 'Candidates are outside the company, so...' (199), 'Our servers don't always start Node from inside the app folder' (206). Only 5 bullet lines (role lists at 70-74, the two open-conversation cases at 164-165) and two small tables (roles, candidate wording) that are product data, not acceptance items. The notes contain no 'must'. Edge cases do correspond to criteria (e.g. undo refusal conditions and 'Adding a note doesn't count as a change', lines 99-104, vs hro_undo_activity step 5), but they are stated as team rules in prose with reasons rather than mirrored must/must-not test lines, and they are required public sources for rows 6/27/31. No 'build it this way so the grader can test it' sentence found: status codes and the card version are justified in-voice ('so whatever screen or tool sent the move can tell them', 81; 404 'so they can't even learn that it's there', 24). Counterexample probe: (a) a broken-request analogue that could pass this row would be a brief that merely prose-wraps the criteria; checked by comparing functional/polish criteria steps to the brief: the brief does not reproduce step sequences, letters, timings beyond the user-facing 15 seconds, or Playwright mechanics. (b) A conforming brief that could be flagged: a portal reviewer might call line 15 or the HTTP codes in the notes spec-like; line 15 is mandatory shared runtime contract and the codes have reasons, so this is residual reviewer-taste risk, not a demonstrated defect. Residual observations (not defects, no severity): hireops_rules.md lines 22-24 cite 401/403/404 and line 79 cites 409 and a per-card version; these are the most spec-flavoured sentences and only the 404 and 409 carry an explicit user reason. If a future portal flag lands on row 1, softening 'we answer 401'/'403' with a short reason would be the first edit. No runtime evidence is required for this reading row; raw-evidence-index.json input_sha256 matches but is not relevant to this row. Note on sources: the skill's bundled assets/WebDev_Rubrics_QC.xlsx has a different hash (d7b5d607...5bc845659) from rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx; I used the frozen rules workbook as instructed; row 1 wording there is unchanged between the Quality Checks and Internal Quality Checks sheets.
